newsitem.title: UK: UK orders expectations highest for 2 years-poll.
newsitem.headline: UK orders expectations highest for 2 years-poll.

text.p: Expectations for new orders in British industry are generally at their highest for two years and confidence in increased sales and profits remains high, according to a Dun & Bradstreet poll.
Its poll of over 1,400 managing directors throughout British business showed the prospect of the opposition Labour party winning the May 1 election had not dented business confidence.
There was only a slight indication of firms increasing selling prices and there were no signs that firms were preparing to shed staff.

"However, fears of a post-election rise in interest rates may have dented the bullishness of wholesalers and retailers, who were among the most optimistic sectors in D & B's previous survey at the beginning of this year," the company said.
The services sector was the most optimistic, while manufacturing and construction firms expected to see increases in sales, profits and new orders.
"The current momentum of the economy appears to be so settled that it won't be fazed by whichever party wins the general election," said Dun & Bradstreet senior analyst Philip Mellor.
"But some sectors of the economy, notably the retailers, are reserving their judgment and waiting to see what happens to interest rates."
